title: Growth Risk, Dollar Strength, and the Bitcoin Liquidity Test
summary: This week raises a different explanation for higher yields: strong nominal growth may matter more than fiscal stress alone. A possible slowdown, uncertain dollar direction, and energy-financing risks make liquidity confirmation more useful than a single monetary narrative.
thesisBullets: Higher yields do not automatically indicate a loss of confidence in government finances; growth expectations and inflation can also drive borrowing costs.
A slowdown could favor government bonds while weakening commodity demand, challenging the assumption that bonds must fall whenever the long-term scarcity case strengthens.
A currency can gain against its peers even while losing domestic purchasing power. Dollar strength and monetary erosion are different questions for Bitcoin investors.

Bond-market volatility can restrict financing capacity, while elevated energy costs can squeeze cash flow. Electricity investment also raises questions about who ultimately carries the financing risk.
btcImplications: Bitcoin could face near-term funding pressure even if its long-term scarcity appeal remains intact.
Falling bond yields would be more encouraging alongside stable credit conditions than alongside a rush out of risky assets.
Look for actual spot demand and orderly financing before treating a macro argument as confirmation for Bitcoin.

factorImplications.weeklyChange: Slowdown and dollar risks in focus

counterThesis: Growth could remain resilient, undermining the slowdown case and keeping upward pressure on yields.
A weaker dollar and easier financing could support Bitcoin before clear improvement in the growth outlook.
Persistent inflation or fiscal concerns could prevent a bond rally even if economic activity slows.
watchNext: Whether yield changes align with growth expectations, inflation concerns, or credit stress.

Bond volatility, collateral availability, and short-term funding conditions.
Energy costs and the financing burden of new electricity infrastructure.
Bitcoin spot demand, holder behavior, and signs of leveraged positioning stress.
whatWouldChange: Easier financing, calmer bond markets, and sustained Bitcoin demand would strengthen the constructive case.
Worsening credit conditions alongside dollar strength would make the liquidity risk more pressing.
Resilient growth with contained energy costs would weaken the slowdown thesis.
